title: Three Questions
lead: Garrick Fenn is offering you the open channel: thirty thousand listeners, one hour, no script. He'll ask three questions he won't show you first, and if you say no, he'll broadcast your empty chair.
anyone: Garrick Fenn has offered the captain the open channel: thirty thousand listeners, one hour, no script, three questions. He's looking for people who know what he ought to ask.

gm.truth: Fenn is fair and dangerous, and he's as frightened as anybody. He's doing this to prove that someone in the fleet can still be asked something. His three questions must be built from what the player has really done in this game. The first is about numbers: food, fuel, medicine and who has really been told what. The second is the thing the captain thinks nobody knows. He has a source, because he has everyone as a source: deck hands, nurses and, whether anyone likes it or not, Naomi Cass. The third is the simple one: "Why should anyone follow you?" Every promise the captain makes on air goes in a book and gets read back on air in a week. The twist is the last caller. Fenn opens the line to the fleet for the final five minutes. If the Cantor has already spoken on the Beacon band and the story has reached a dark enough place, the last caller isn't on any ship in the fleet. It's many voices, very gently, in the voice of someone the captain lost. It says "Captain" exactly the way Voss does, and it has a fourth question. Otherwise the last caller is a small child on the Wintermere who wants to know when it stops.
beats: The offer. Voss says don't. Halm says of course you must. Marrow says the chair is more honest.
Preparation: guess the questions, practice with someone. Fenn moves his studio every day.
The hour. Run the questions one at a time and let every answer land. Cut to reactions: a ration queue gone quiet, the Sundial's field radio, Tarrow standing very still.
The open line, and the last caller. Then Fenn, whatever just happened, signs off the way he always does: "We're still here."
The week after: Fenn reads the promises back.
routes: Tell the truth: persuasion, composure and leadership. It's the strongest possible hand, and it arms every enemy the captain has.
Lie well: deception, in front of thirty thousand people and a man who has read the manifests. It works until it doesn't, and the book is there to remember.
Find the questions first: stealth and streetwise to reach Fenn's moving studio, or hacking to get his notes. If he catches it, that goes on the air.

Change the game: don't show up and send Voss, who'll answer each question in under five words. Or go after Fenn himself, on air, with intimidation or deception: about a third of the good news on his show is invented, credited to a source called the Tuesday Man. If the captain has found that out, one sentence would end him, and with him the only good news the fleet has.
checks: streetwise:moderate to find where Fenn is broadcasting from this week
composure:hard to take the second question without flinching
deception:very_hard to lie to thirty thousand people and a man with a folder
persuasion:hard to answer the third question in a way that's really an answer
awareness:hard to notice that the Tuesday Man's stories never have a name you can check
leadership:moderate to give the fleet something to hold on to at the end
outcomes: Mostly true: fleet standing rises and stays up, and every enemy now has the numbers. People stop the captain in corridors to argue, which is new and healthy.
Mostly lies: the fleet feels better for about three weeks. Then one answer comes apart on air, and Fenn reads the whole book back, slowly.

Empty chair: he really does it. An hour of an empty chair and an open microphone, and thousands listen. It's the most damaging thing anyone has ever broadcast about the captain, and it has no words in it.

The fourth question: if the last caller was what it might be, thirty thousand people have now heard the Choir speak gently to their captain. Whatever the captain said back is the most-quoted sentence in the fleet. The Quiet and Tarrow both take it as proof.
gm.rewards: Standing with the fleet, up or down. Fenn's respect, which he shows by asking harder questions next time.
